meta.description: Combat actions, defense actions, free actions, maneuvers, and special combat situations for TDE4/DSA4.1. Entries that were previously extracted from the TDE4e wiki fandom page are intentionally left untouched. Non-wiki entries and newly added entries are enriched in English from Wege des Schwerts.
source_books: Wege des Schwerts p. 58–72: Kampfaktionen und Manöver
Wege des Schwerts p. 78–86: optionale Kampfregeln / special combat situations
Wege des Schwerts p. 100–107: mounted combat and related rules

the_call_rules.description:
The Call.

Many maneuvers let the fighter voluntarily make their own Attack or Parry harder. This self-chosen penalty is called a Call. Fixed maneuver penalties, such as the basic penalty for a Stun Blow with a club, are also counted as part of the maneuver's total penalty.

Limits:
- The total penalty may not exceed the Talent Prowess of the weapon used.
- The total penalty may not exceed the relevant Attack or Parry Value.
- For offensive maneuvers, use the Attack Value.
- For defensive maneuvers, use the Parry Value.

Failed Call:
- If a maneuver with a Call fails, the fighter suffers the full failed Call as a penalty.
- This penalty applies to all tests until the fighter uses their next Attack or Parry action.
- It also applies to Free Actions that require tests during that time.
- Once the next Attack or Parry action is used, the penalty is cleared.

Blade Dancer:
- A fighter with the Blade Dancer Special Ability suffers only half the declared points as the failed Call penalty.

Example:
- A fighter fails a Called Attack with a Call of 5.
- Their next Parry, Attack, or test-based Free Action is penalized by 5.
- After that next Attack or Parry action is used, the penalty no longer applies.

attack_actions.name: Standard Attack
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action.

A standard attack is the basic offensive combat action. The attacker uses the opening offered by the opponent to strike or thrust without trying to create a special additional effect.

Resolution:
- Roll 1d20 against the attacker's Attack Value, modified only by the situation, weapon, distance class, lighting, position, and similar ordinary modifiers.
- If the Attack succeeds, the defender must use a valid defense action such as Parry, shield parry, parrying-weapon parry, or Dodge.
- If the defender's defense fails or is unavailable, the target is hit and damage is resolved normally.
- If the Attack fails, it does not necessarily mean the blow visibly misses; it may have been delayed, poorly placed, deflected by clothing or armor, or otherwise harmless.

Limits:
- A normal attack has no Call and creates no additional wound, knockdown, disarm, or positioning effect by itself.
- Special attack maneuvers replace or modify this basic action.

attack_actions.name: Blade Storm
attack_actions.shield_restriction: no shield (except parrying weapons that count as shields)
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action.

Blade Storm allows a trained fighter to split one Attack Action between two opponents. It is useful when fighting several weaker defenders, but it requires the Blade Storm Special Ability and a suitable weapon.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Daggers
- Fencing Weapons
- Infantry Weapons
- Sabers
- Swords
- Spears
- Staves

Restrictions:
- The attacker may not carry a shield, except shields that also count as Parrying Weapons.
- Maximum Encumbrance is EC 4.
- Both targets must already be within the attacker's ideal distance class.
- The maneuver cannot be combined with another attack maneuver.
- A converted Parry Action cannot be split this way.
- An additional attack from an off-hand weapon cannot be split this way.

Resolution:
- The attacker makes two attacks, one after the other.
- Each attack uses half the attacker's Attack Value, plus 2.
- Example: Attack Value 15 becomes two attacks at Attack Value 10.
- The normal rules for fighting multiple opponents still apply.
- The attacker cannot concentrate only on one opponent.

Special cases:
- With Combat Awareness, the improved Attack Value may be distributed freely between two attacks, but each attack must receive at least 6 points.
- With Blade Dancer, the attack may be split between up to three opponents.

attack_actions.name: Blunt Blow
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +2/+4/+8.

Blunt Blow is used when the attacker wants to disable or subdue an opponent instead of killing or seriously injuring them. The attacker strikes with a blunt side, pommel, club-like part of the weapon, or a suitable brawling weapon.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Brawling, only with a brawling weapon or weapon pommel
- Sabers
- Swords
- Staves

Attack penalty:
- +2 with combat staves and clubs.
- +4 with axes or maces that have a usable flat side.
- +8 with other eligible weapons.

Effect:
- Strength-based damage modifiers still apply.
- The attack causes Endurance Damage Points instead of normal weapon damage.
- A fighter with the Stun Blow Special Ability halves the listed attack penalties.
- A brawling attack with a weapon pommel normally causes real damage, unless the attacker has Stun Blow and uses it as a Blunt Blow.

attack_actions.name: Called Attack
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action + Call.

Called Attack is a forceful strike. The attacker accepts a self-chosen penalty to the Attack test in exchange for increased damage if the blow lands.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Infantry Weapons
- Chain Weapons
- Brawling
- Wrestling
- Sabers
- Swords
- Staves
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Declaration:
- Before rolling, the attacker declares the Call.
- The Call may not exceed the attacker's Talent Prowess with the weapon.
- The Call may not exceed the Attack Value being used.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and the defender fails to parry, half the Call is added to Damage Points.
- Round the half Call up.
- If the attacker has the Called Attack Special Ability, the full Call is added instead.
- Severe Hit and Wound rules apply normally.

Effect on failure:
- A failed Called Attack causes the normal failed Call penalty.
- Until the next Attack or Parry action is used, the fighter's tests are penalized by the full Call.
- This also affects Free Actions that require tests.

Related maneuvers:
- Called Attack is the basis for several stronger maneuvers, including Cleave Attack, Stun Blow, Hammer Strike, Knockdown, Shield Splitter, and similar force-based techniques.

attack_actions.name: Charge
attack_actions.damage_bonus_on_success: half of Base Speed + 4 + optional Call
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +4; also consumes the Parry Action.

Charge combines movement and attack into one powerful opening strike. It is usually used to start melee, because after the first clash there may not be enough room for another run-up.

Requirements:
- Requires the Charge Special Ability.
- The attacker must have Base Speed 4 or higher, after Encumbrance is considered.
- The attacker must be able to make at least a 4-pace run-up.
- The attacker gives up the Parry Action for the game turn.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Infantry Weapons
- Chain Weapons
- Sabers
- Swords
- Spears
- Staves
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Resolution:
- The Attack test is penalized by +4.
- Because this is a Called Attack variant, the attacker may add another Call for more damage.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and the defender cannot parry or dodge, damage increases.
- Add half the attacker's Base Speed.
- Add another +4 Damage Points.
- Add any declared Call used for damage.
- The Charge ends at the distance class chosen by the attacker, normally the optimal distance of the attacker's weapon.

Counterplay:
- If the defender has a longer-distance weapon and the appropriate Special Ability, they may attempt Counter.
- This represents making the charging attacker run onto the defender's weapon.

Effect on failure:
- The defender may immediately make a Free Attack.
- The attacker has still spent the Parry Action for the game turn.
- The attacker may also suffer the failed Call penalty.
- If the defender's desired distance class is longer than the attacker's target distance, the attacker remains at the defender's distance class.

attack_actions.name: Cleave Attack
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +4 per additional opponent; consumes Parry Action
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +4 per opponent; also consumes the Parry Action.

Cleave Attack is a sweeping blow against several nearby opponents. The fighter turns the attack through a wide arc, striking up to three targets one after another.

Requirements:
- Requires the Cleave Attack Special Ability.
- The fighter must give up the Parry Action for the round.
- The maneuver cannot be used if the fighter has already spent the reaction elsewhere.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Infantry Weapons
- Chain Weapons
- Sabers
- Swords
- Staves
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Resolution:
- The Attack test is penalized by +4 per opponent.
- Because this is a Called Attack variant, the attacker may add another Call.
- If the attack succeeds, each defender rolls their own Parry.

Use of the additional Call:
- The Call may increase Damage Points against every target hit.
- If the attacker also has Feint, the Call may instead penalize all defenders' Parries or Dodges.
- The attacker may split the Call between damage increase and Parry/Dodge penalty.

Effects on each failed Parry:
- The target is hit and may suffer wounds normally.
- The target is driven back one distance class.
- The target loses 1d6 Initiative.
- The attack also counts as an automatic Knockdown Attack.
- If the target cannot step back, they suffer 1d6 additional damage.

attack_actions.name: Death Blow
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +8 + half opponent AR + optional Call; consumes Parry Action
attack_actions.failure_consequence: Defender gets a Free Attack; attacker loses Parry Action for this turn; failed Call penalty applies
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +8 + half the opponent's AR + Call; also consumes the Parry Action.

Death Blow is a high-risk thrust meant to decide a fight with one precise, lethal attack. It is the thrusting-weapon counterpart to Hammer Strike.

Requirements:
- Requires the Death Blow Special Ability.
- The attacker must give up the Parry Action.
- The Parry Action must be given up no later than the attacker's Initiative Phase.
- If the attacker has already used a Parry Action this game turn, Death Blow is not possible.

Usable with:
- Daggers
- Fencing Weapons
- Swords, if the attacker also knows Half-Sword
- Spears

Attack penalty:
- Base penalty is +8.
- Add half the defender's Armor Rating.
- If the defender carries a shield, add the shield's Parry modifier to the attack penalty.
- The attacker may add a further Call as a Feint to penalize the defender's Parry.
- If the attacker has Called Attack, Call points may also be assigned to damage increase, even if the weapon normally does not allow Called Attack.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and is not parried, armor is ignored when calculating Damage Points.
- Natural armor is not ignored.
- The defender's Wound Threshold is reduced by 2 for this attack.
- The defender automatically suffers two additional wounds.

Effect on failure:
- The defender receives a Free Attack.
- The attacker has still spent the Parry Action for the game turn.
- The attacker suffers the failed Call penalty from +8 plus any voluntary Call.

Restriction:
- Death Blow cannot be used against very large creatures.

attack_actions.name: Double Attack
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +2 per attack; +4 for non-identical weapons; -3 for off-hand without Ambidextrous Combat II
restrictions: both weapons must be usable in the same distance class without penalty
cannot combine with Supplemental Action from Ambidextrous Combat II or Parrying Weapons II or Death from the Left in same turn
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +2.

Double Attack lets a fighter strike one opponent with both weapons at almost the same time. The goal is to force the defender to deal with two separate blows in a single Initiative Phase.

Requirements:
- Requires the Double Attack Special Ability.
- Requires Ambidextrous Combat I.
- Both weapons must be usable in the same distance class without penalty.

Usable with:
- All one-handed weapons except Chain Weapons and Spears.

Restrictions:
- The maneuver is always directed against one opponent.
- A converted Parry Action cannot be used for a Double Attack.
- It cannot be used in the same game turn as a Supplemental Action from Ambidextrous Combat II.
- It cannot be used in the same game turn as a Supplemental Action from Parrying Weapons II.
- It cannot be used in the same game turn as Death from the Left.

Attack penalties:
- Both attacks are penalized by +2.
- If the weapons are not identical, the off-hand attack suffers an additional +4 penalty.
- The normal off-hand penalty also applies unless the fighter has Ambidextrous Combat II.

Resolution:
- Roll both attacks separately.
- Neither partial attack may be another maneuver.
- The maneuver may conclude a Lunge.
- It may benefit from a preceding Master Parry.
- If one partial attack is a Fumble, the other partial attack automatically fails too.

Defense:
- The defender must spend two Parries to block both blows.
- This can come from prepared conversion, Foresight, Defensive Combat Style, Wall of Blades, or off-hand Supplemental Actions.
- Alternatively, the defender may use a Targeted Dodge to leave the reach of both blows.
- If the attacks hit and are not parried, roll and apply the damage from each weapon separately.

attack_actions.name: Feint
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action + Call.

Feint is a deceptive attack. The attacker threatens one body zone, then redirects the weapon to create a harder-to-defend opening.

Usable with:
- All armed melee talents except Chain Weapons and Two-Handed Blunt Weapons.

Restrictions:
- The attacker must be agile enough to perform the maneuver.
- Encumbrance may not exceed EC 4, after relevant reductions such as Armor Use.
- Carrying a shield adds another +2 penalty because it restricts mobility.
- The shield penalty does not apply to small shields.

Declaration:
- Before rolling, the attacker declares a Call.
- The Call may not exceed the attacker's Talent Prowess with the weapon.
- The Call may not exceed the Attack Value being used.

Effect on success:
- The Call does not increase damage.
- Instead, it penalizes the defender's Parry or Dodge.
- Without the Feint Special Ability, the defender suffers half the Call as a penalty.
- With the Feint Special Ability, the defender suffers the full Call as a penalty.
- If the defense fails, damage is rolled normally.

Combinations:
- Feint can sometimes be combined with Called Attack.
- In such cases, the Call may be split between Parry penalty and damage increase.
- Bonus points from Master Parry or Bind may be used for the Feint.

Effect on failure:
- If the Attack itself fails, the attacker suffers the normal failed Call penalty.

Prerequisite role:
- Feint is a prerequisite for several maneuvers, including Lunge, Stun Blow, Targeted Thrust, Blade Storm, Death Blow, and Trip.

attack_actions.name: Hammer Strike
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +8 + optional Call; consumes ALL actions for the round (not Free Actions)
restrictions: not against opponents carrying a large or very large shield
attack_actions.failure_consequence: Defender gets a Free Attack the attacker cannot block
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +8 + Call; consumes all actions of the current round.

Hammer Strike is a full-commitment attack meant to overwhelm an opponent with one devastating blow.

Requirements:
- Requires the Hammer Strike Special Ability.
- The attacker must give up all other actions in the current round, except Free Actions.
- If forced to parry before their Initiative Phase, the attacker must choose between the Parry and the Hammer Strike.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords, except Nightwind
- Axes and Maces
- Infantry Weapons
- Chain Weapons
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Resolution:
- The Attack test is penalized by +8.
- Because this is a Called Attack variant, the attacker may add another Call to increase damage.
- The maneuver may be combined with a Feint to penalize the defender's Parry.

Effect on success:
- The defender may attempt an unmodified Parry.
- If the Parry fails, the rolled Damage Points are tripled.
- Any Call assigned to damage increase is also tripled.
- If the defender parries a Hammer Strike with an added Call of +2 or more, a Break Test may be triggered.

Restrictions:
- Hammer Strike cannot be used against very large opponents.
- It cannot be used against opponents carrying a large or very large shield.

Effect on failure:
- The defender receives a Free Attack.
- The attacker cannot block that Free Attack.

attack_actions.name: Knockdown
attack_actions.sabers_restriction: only Arbach, Haumesser, Khunchomer, and Sklaventod
attack_actions.extra_damage_condition: if Damage Points exceed defender's ST, excess applies as additional penalty to ST test
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +4 + Call.

Knockdown is a forceful blow meant to stagger the target or throw them to the ground.

Requirements:
- Requires the Knockdown Special Ability.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Infantry Weapons
- Chain Weapons
- Sabers, only Arbach, Haumesser, Khunchomer, and Sklaventod
- Swords
- Staves
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Resolution:
- The Attack test is penalized by +4.
- Because this is a Called Attack variant, the attacker may add another Call.
- In this maneuver, the voluntary Call does not increase damage.
- Instead, the Call penalizes the defender's Strength test.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and is not parried, the defender suffers normal weapon damage.
- The defender must then pass a Strength test to remain standing.
- Steady Stand eases this test by 1.
- Balance eases this test by 2.
- Outstanding Balance eases this test by 4.

If the Strength test succeeds:
- The defender remains standing.
- The defender loses 1d6 Initiative.

If the Strength test fails:
- The defender falls prone.
- The defender loses 2d6 Initiative.
- In grid combat, the defender falls into the adjacent square away from the attacker.
- The defender then suffers the normal disadvantages of being prone.

Additional penalty:
- If one blow causes more Damage Points than the defender's Strength, the excess Damage Points are added as an extra penalty to the Strength test.

Restrictions and notes:
- Knockdown cannot be combined with another Attack Action except Charge.
- It can use points from a preceding Master Parry.
- A successful Parry against Knockdown may trigger a Break Test.

attack_actions.name: Shield Splitter
attack_actions.call_effect: penalizes defender's Parry (if attacker has Feint SA) or reduces Break Test
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +8 minus the shield's Parry Value modifier.

Shield Splitter is an attack directed at the opponent's shield rather than the opponent. It aims to break, splinter, or deform the shield so it can no longer protect its bearer.

Requirements:
- Requires the Shield Splitter Special Ability.

Usable with:
- Axes and Maces
- Chain Weapons
- Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
- Two-Handed Swords

Resolution:
- The Attack test is penalized by +8.
- The penalty is reduced by the shield's Parry Value bonus, because a larger shield is easier to hit.
- The attacker may declare an additional Call.

Use of the additional Call:
- If the attacker has Feint, the Call may penalize the shield-bearer's Parry.
- Otherwise, or instead, the Call may be subtracted from the following Break Test.
- The Call does not increase damage to the shield-bearer.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and the defender fails the shield Parry, the shield must immediately make a Break Test.
- Subtract 4 plus any additional Call from the 2d6 Break Test roll.
- If the Break Test fails, the shield is destroyed and grants no further protection.
- The shield-bearer takes no direct damage from this maneuver.
- If the Break Test succeeds, the shield gains 1 Break Point.
- If the Break Test roll is 12, the attacker's weapon must also immediately make a Break Test.

attack_actions.name: Stun Blow
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +2 / +4 / +8 depending on weapon + optional Call
attack_actions.unconsciousness_trigger: Endurance loss > Wound Threshold: CN test; Endurance loss > CN: automatic unconscious for 1d6 turns
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +2/+4/+8 + Call.

Stun Blow combines Blunt Blow and Called Attack. It is used to incapacitate a target through Endurance loss instead of normal killing damage.

Requirements:
- Requires the Stun Blow Special Ability.
- The weapon must have a usable blunt side or striking surface.

Usable with:
- Bastard Swords
- Axes and Maces
- Brawling, only with brawling weapons or a weapon pommel
- Sabers
- Swords
- Staves

Attack penalty:
- +2 with combat staves and blunt maces or clubs.
- +4 with the blunt side of other axes and maces.
- +8 with all other eligible weapons.

Effect:
- Damage is tracked as Endurance Damage Points.
- The maneuver may be combined with Called Attack or Feint.
- Bonus points from Master Parry or Bind may be used.

Pommel or brawling use:
- A fighter with Stun Blow may try to incapacitate an opponent with a weapon pommel.
- This is a Brawling Attack penalized by +4.
- The attacker must be close enough to strike this way, usually Melee Distance Class if distance classes are used.

Incapacitation:
- If one blow causes Endurance loss greater than the target's Wound Threshold, the target must pass a Constitution test.
- On a failed Constitution test, the target falls unconscious for 1d6 game turns.
- If the Endurance loss is greater than the target's Constitution, unconsciousness is automatic.
- A wound may still occur if the real Damage Points exceed the target's Wound Threshold.

Restrictions:
- Stun Blow only works against creatures that can be stunned.
- It does not work against undead, demons, and many creatures without a skull or comparable anatomy, such as slimes or kraken.
- Against animals, the attacker should succeed at an Animal Lore test to judge the anatomy correctly; the penalty is set by the GM according to the animal.

attack_actions.name: Targeted Thrust
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +4 + half opponent AR + optional Call
restrictions: only against creatures with discernible vulnerable points (not most demons, slime creatures, most undead)
attack_actions.shield_penalty: shield Parry modifier added to AT penalty
attack_actions.failure_consequence: equivalent to failed Call of 4 + optional Call
attack_actions.description:
Attack Action +4 + half the opponent's AR + Call.

Targeted Thrust is a precise attack with a thrusting weapon. It aims for a vulnerable point, bypassing armor and increasing the chance of a serious wound.

Requirements:
- Requires the Targeted Thrust Special Ability.

Usable with:
- Daggers
- Fencing Weapons
- Swords, if the attacker also knows Half-Sword
- Spears

Attack penalty:
- Base penalty is +4.
- Add half the defender's Armor Rating.
- If the defender carries a shield, add the shield's Parry modifier to the attack penalty.
- The attacker may add a further Call to penalize the defender's Parry.

Effect on success:
- If the Attack succeeds and is not parried, the attack hits a vulnerable point.
- Armor is ignored.
- Natural armor is also ignored.
- Hit Points are effectively Damage Points.
- The defender's Wound Threshold is reduced by 2 for this attack.
- The defender automatically suffers one additional wound.

Effect on failure:
- A failed Targeted Thrust counts as a failed Call of 4 plus any voluntary Call.

Restriction:
- Targeted Thrust only works against creatures with recognizable vulnerable points.
- It usually cannot be used against most demons, slime creatures, or most undead.

attack_actions.name: Assault
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +4 to initiate; continued attacks convert defense actions without normal conversion penalty
attack_actions.description:
Attack Maneuver +4 to initiate.

Assault is an aggressive sequence of attacks meant to force the opponent into pure defense. The attacker presses forward with repeated blows or thrusts, trying to keep the defender retreating until a decisive attack, Feint, or similar maneuver creates the opening.

Requirements:
- Requires the Assault Special Ability.
- Usable with Bastard Swords, Daggers, Fencing Weapons, Chain Staves, Sabers, Swords, Spears, and Staves.
- Both fighters must be in a suitable distance class; the attacker normally begins from the weapon's ideal distance.

Resolution:
- The first Attack is penalized by +4, plus all other normal modifiers.
- If it succeeds, the defender is forced into defense and can no longer make normal attacks while the Assault continues.
- Each round the attacker converts the defense action into another attack without the usual conversion penalty.
- Each attack is combined with a Free Action Step forward.
- The defender is likewise forced to convert their own attacks into defenses and to step back, also without the normal conversion penalty unless their weapon normally forbids conversion; in that case the defender suffers +4.
- The defender retreats even if the attacker's actual Attack roll fails, as long as the Assault sequence remains in effect according to the maneuver rules.

Allowed follow-up maneuvers:
- Wuchtschlag/Called Attack and Feint are generally possible during an Assault.
- More complex maneuvers depend on the listed maneuver permissions and GM adjudication.

Ending the Assault:
- It can end when the attacker fails in a way that breaks the pressure, when the defender successfully uses a permitted countermeasure such as Targeted Dodge, when distance or terrain prevents further pressing, or when another listed condition in the combat rules applies.

attack_actions.name: Disarm
attack_actions.description:
Attack Maneuver +8 + Call.

Disarm is a special attack aimed at the opponent's weapon arm, grip, or an exposed part of the weapon. It tries to knock, twist, or tear the weapon from the opponent's hand without causing damage.

Requirements:
- Requires Feint and Disarm.
- The attacker may not carry a shield because many disarming techniques need the second hand.
- Usable with Bastard Swords, Fencing Weapons, Infantry Weapons, Chain Staves, Whips, Sabers, Swords, Spears, Staves, and Two-Handed Swords/Sabers when using Half-Sword.
- Fencing Weapons can disarm only other Fencing Weapons or Daggers.

Resolution:
- Make an Attack +8.
- If the defender's Parry fails, the defender may still keep the weapon by succeeding at a Strength test +8.
- Against a fighter with Masterful Disarm, the Strength test is +10.
- The target suffers no damage from the maneuver.

Modifiers and combinations:
- A combat staff eases the Disarm attack by 2.
- A chain staff or two-lilies weapon eases it by 4.
- The maneuver can be combined with Feint by adding a voluntary Call.
- The voluntary Call can penalize the defender's Parry and/or the later Strength test.
- Bonus points from Master Parry or Bind can be used if the maneuver allows them.

Two-handed weapons:
- Disarming a target using a two-handed weapon, except Bastard Swords, requires Masterful Disarm.
- Sabers cannot be used for this special case.

attack_actions.name: Pin Down
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +4 + optional Call; consumes defense action
attack_actions.description:
Attack Maneuver +4 + Call; consumes the defense action.

Pin Down uses a straight-bladed polearm with a crosspiece or similar stop to pierce and lever the victim, drag them down, and hold them on the ground while their strength fades. It is especially associated with big-game hunting and is brutal but effective against oversized dangerous enemies.

Requirements:
- Requires the Pin Down Special Ability.
- Usable only with suitable polearms such as trident, Efferdbart, elven hunting spear, hunting spear, boar spear, partisan, thrusting spear, and wurm spear.

Resolution:
- The attacker makes Attack +4 and may add a voluntary Call.
- If the attack succeeds, the weapon deals normal weapon damage, not increased by the voluntary Call.
- A comparative Agility test determines whether the weapon stays set for the maneuver.
- If the defender wins the Agility comparison, they free themselves but suffer an additional one-time 1d6 damage points.
- If the attacker wins, a comparative Strength test follows to see whether the victim is thrown down.
- The attacker receives a point pool equal to twice the voluntary Call to improve these comparison results.

If the attacker wins the Strength comparison:
- The victim is prone and held by the attacker.
- In the following combat rounds the weapon automatically deals its damage again, without Calls and without TP/ST.
- Each round a new comparative Strength test is made; the victim is penalized by +2.
- Remaining points from the original pool may still be used.

Multiple attackers:
- Several attackers can delay actions to Pin Down in the same Initiative phase.
- Each additional successful attacker eases the comparative tests by 2.
- The comparisons are still resolved separately for each attacker.

Already prone or held targets:
- If the victim is already prone, no comparative Agility test is needed; only Strength is compared.
- If the victim is already held down by another fighter, no comparison is needed and the Pin Down attack is not penalized.

Restrictions:
- While holding the victim, the attacker can do nothing else but spend actions maintaining the hold.
- The victim can do nothing except spend actions trying to shake off the attacker.

attack_actions.name: Trip
attack_actions.base_modifier: AT +4 + optional Call; no increased damage
attack_actions.description:
Attack Maneuver +4 + Call.

Trip is used to tear an opponent off balance with a hook, shaft, chain, whip, or similar weapon action. Unlike a pure force-based Knockdown, it relies more on leverage and destabilization than raw damage.

Requirements:
- Requires the Trip Special Ability.
- Usually used with weapons suited to hooking, sweeping, or pulling, such as Chain Staves, Chain Weapons, Whips, Spears, and Staves, depending on the weapon list and GM ruling.

Resolution:
- The attacker makes an Attack +4 and may add a voluntary Call.
- If the attack succeeds and is not parried, the target suffers the normal weapon effect and must resist being pulled or thrown down.
- The voluntary Call does not increase damage; it penalizes the target's resistance test.
- On failure, the target falls prone and suffers the normal penalties for prone fighters.

Notes:
- The maneuver is less useful against creatures that cannot reasonably be tripped because of size, many legs, amorphous anatomy, flight, or supernatural stability.
- The GM should adjust or forbid it against animals, demons, undead, and very large monsters when their body shape makes the maneuver implausible.

defense_actions.name: Parry
defense_actions.description:
Defense Action.

A standard Parry is the basic way to defend against a melee attack with the fighter's own weapon. It represents blocking, redirecting, letting a blow slide off the weapon, and using body movement and counter-threats to keep the attacker at a safe distance.

Resolution:
- The defender must choose the defense type before rolling.
- Roll 1d20 against the relevant Parry Value, modified by weapon, shield, distance class, situation, wounds, encumbrance, and maneuver penalties.
- If the Parry succeeds, the attack is deflected and causes no damage.
- If the Parry fails, the attack hits and damage is resolved normally.
- A roll of 1 may be a lucky parry, with possible additional effects depending on the optional critical/parry rules.

Restrictions and notes:
- Some attacks or situations may forbid Parry, require a different defense, or add special modifiers.
- The defender cannot wait to see the result and then change to a different defense type.
- Shields and parrying weapons use their own detailed rules when chosen instead of a weapon Parry.

defense_actions.name: Evade
defense_actions.description:
Defense Action / Free Defense Action.

Evade means getting out of the reach of an incoming attack instead of stopping it with a weapon or shield. Wege des Schwerts distinguishes ordinary Evade from Targeted Evade.

Ordinary Evade:
- Ordinary Evade is a Free defense action.
- On success, the defender completely avoids the attack.
- Against several opponents, it avoids only one attack; the defender may still be threatened by other attacks.
- The defender becomes somewhat disoriented: Initiative is reduced by 4.
- The defender must spend an Action Position before actively rejoining the fight; until then, they can only continue evading.
- On failure, the defender is hit and also loses 4 Initiative.

Targeted Evade:
- Targeted Evade is a standard defense action, comparable to Parry.
- The evade test uses double the distance-class penalty, plus the normal values of other modifiers.
- On success, the defender avoids the attack completely and can continue fighting normally.
- Against several opponents, it still avoids only one attack unless a specific rule says otherwise.
- On failure, the defender is hit as after a failed Parry and loses 2 Initiative.
- Targeted Evade can be used with a voluntary Call; on success this functions like a Master Parry, while failure has the normal failed Call consequences.
- Targeted Evade can end an opponent's Ausfall/Assault.

Typical evade modifiers:
- Distance Class Handgemenge: +4.
- Distance Class Nahkampf: +2.
- Distance Class Stangenwaffe: +1.
- Distance Class Pike: +0.
- Targeted Evade: distance-class modifier is doubled.
- Each additional opponent: +2.
- Surrounded by 4 or more opponents: impossible.
- Encumbrance: +EC.
- Evade I / II / III Special Abilities reduce the penalty by 3 / 6 / 9.
- Athletics Talent Prowess can reduce the penalty: every 3 TP above 9 gives -1.

defense_actions.name: Master Parry
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver + Call.

Master Parry is an improved Parry in which the defender deliberately makes the defense harder in order to gain an advantage for the next action.

Declaration:
- Before rolling the Parry, the defender declares a voluntary Call.
- The Call may not exceed the fighter's Talent Prowess with the weapon and may not exceed the Parry Value used.
- The maneuver requires the Master Parry Special Ability.

Effect on success:
- The Parry stops the attack normally.
- The declared Call becomes bonus points for the defender's next Attack or for certain follow-up maneuvers that explicitly allow these points.
- The bonus may be used, for example, to ease the defender's next attack, to support a Feint, or to power compatible maneuver effects.
- The exact follow-up must still obey the rules of the selected maneuver and weapon.

Effect on failure:
- The attack hits normally.
- The defender suffers the normal failed Call penalty: all tests until the next Attack or Parry action are penalized by the full declared Call.

Notes:
- A Master Parry is still a defense action and requires an incoming attack.
- Some defensive forms, such as certain shield or parrying-weapon options, restrict whether Master Parry may be used.

defense_actions.name: Bind
defense_actions.base_modifier: PA +4 or opponent Call, whichever is higher; optional extra Call possible with Master Parry
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver +4.

Bind is a central fencing maneuver. The defender catches and maintains contact with the opponent's weapon, using strength and technique to control the weapon line. This improves the defender's next attack while making the opponent's next reaction worse.

Requirements:
- Requires the Bind Special Ability.
- Also requires either Master Parry or Parrying Weapons I, depending on how the bind is performed.
- Can be used with Bastard Swords, Daggers, Fencing Weapons, Infantry Weapons, Chain Staves, Sabers, Swords, Spears, Staves, and parrying weapons.
- It cannot bind Axes and Maces, Chain Staves, Chain Weapons, Whips, Two-Handed Flails, Two-Handed Blunt Weapons, or Two-Handed Swords/Sabers.
- It can be used against shield fighters, but it binds only one weapon or shield-line; a second weapon or parrying weapon remains free.

Resolution:
- The defender makes a Parry +4.
- If the incoming attack has a Call higher than 4, the Bind Parry is instead penalized by that higher Call.
- If the defender binds with the main weapon and has Master Parry, they may add a voluntary Call.
- If the defender binds with a parrying weapon and Parrying Weapons I, the fixed penalty usually counts as the Call without further increasing the roll.
- If the defender has both methods and uses both weapons together, the fixed penalty and voluntary Call add together into one total Call.

Effect on success:
- The defender controls and obstructs the enemy weapon.
- The defender's next Attack is eased by the total Call.
- The opponent's following reaction against that attack is penalized by the same total Call.
- These points can combine with a follow-up Feint or other compatible maneuver.

Effect on failure:
- The incoming attack is not parried.
- The defender suffers the normal failed Call penalty.

defense_actions.name: Counter
defense_actions.description: When an opponent executes a Charge and the defender wields a weapon with a greater reach/distance class and possesses the appropriate SA, they may attempt to make the charging opponent run onto their weapon. Requires the Counter special ability.

defense_actions.name: Foresight
defense_actions.description:
Defense Option.

Foresight represents preparing defensive timing early enough to answer multiple incoming blows, especially attacks that would otherwise arrive too close together.

Use:
- The fighter converts their available defensive planning into multiple separate defense opportunities before the attacks are resolved.
- This is especially relevant against simultaneous or near-simultaneous attacks such as Double Attack.
- The defender must have the appropriate Special Ability and must declare the conversion in time, before the relevant attacks are resolved.

Effect:
- The fighter may defend with two separate Parries instead of being limited to a single ordinary defense.
- Each Parry is resolved separately against one incoming attack.
- The usual limits for converted actions, available actions, distance, weapon restrictions, and maneuver restrictions still apply.

Notes:
- Foresight does not by itself grant unlimited defenses.
- It is a planning and timing tool, not a damage-reduction rule.
- Other rules such as Defensive Combat Style, Blade Wall, extra parrying-weapon parries, or shield-parry options may provide different ways to handle multiple attacks.

defense_actions.name: Defensive Combat Style
defense_actions.base_modifier: no normal conversion penalty when converting Attack to Parry
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver.

Defensive Combat Style is used when survival is more important than attacking, for example while waiting for help, buying time, or facing a foe the fighter cannot currently hurt.

Requirements:
- Requires the Defensive Combat Style Special Ability.
- Usable with all armed melee talents except Chain Weapons and Two-Handed Flails.
- Must be declared at the beginning of the combat round.

Effect:
- The fighter makes no own attacks and concentrates on defense.
- The fighter may convert the Attack action into a Parry without the normal conversion penalty.
- This allows two regular defenses in the round: two Parries, two Targeted Dodges, or one of each, subject to normal limits.
- Each defense still applies only against one incoming attack; a Double Attack counts as two attacks.
- The first of the two Parries may be a Master Parry if otherwise legal.
- Dodge maneuvers used to disengage from an opponent are eased by 2.

Extra actions:
- An additional defense action from a shield or off-hand weapon can still be used normally.
- An additional attack from an off-hand weapon is lost and cannot be converted.

defense_actions.name: Disarm from Parry
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver +8 + Call.

Disarm from Parry is a Master Parry variant. The defender stops the incoming blow and simultaneously attempts to knock or wrench the attacker's weapon from their hand.

Requirements:
- Requires Disarm plus either Master Parry or Parrying Weapons I, depending on the method.
- The defender may not carry a shield because many disarming techniques require the second hand.
- Usable with Bastard Swords, Fencing Weapons, Infantry Weapons, Chain Staves, Sabers, Swords, Spears, Staves, and Two-Handed Swords/Sabers with Half-Sword.
- Fencing Weapons can be used only against other Fencing Weapons or Daggers.
- Parrying weapons such as buckler, hook dagger, left-hand dagger, or suitable dragon claw can also be used with Parrying Weapons I.

Resolution:
- The defender rolls Parry +8.
- If successful, the attacker may keep the weapon with a Strength test +8.
- Against Masterful Disarm, the Strength test is +10.
- If the defender added a voluntary Call, that Call further penalizes the attacker's Strength test.

Parrying weapon modifiers:
- Buckler, hook dagger, left-hand dagger, or suitable dragon claw ease the maneuver by 2.

Two-handed weapons:
- Disarming a two-handed weapon, except Bastard Swords, requires Masterful Disarm.
- Sabers cannot be used for that case.
- Among parrying weapons, only buckler and hook dagger can be used for that case.

defense_actions.name: Formation Parry
defense_actions.base_modifier: special; formation members may parry for adjacent allies
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver.

Formation allows a trained group standing shoulder to shoulder with similar weapons to act as a defensive unit. With one-handed weapons and shields this is often a shield wall.

Requirements:
- All participating fighters must know Formation.
- Usable with Infantry Weapons, Spears, Two-Handed Swords/Sabers, and Shields.
- The fighters must actually stand in formation, normally adjacent to one another.
- Entering formation when already next to each other requires an Action Position.

Effect:
- A formation member can parry an attack aimed at themselves, the ally to the left, or the ally to the right.
- The defender must declare whether they will attempt to parry after a successful attack against themselves or a neighbor.
- This consumes the defender's defense action for the round whether or not the Parry is later needed and whether or not it succeeds.
- Declarations and Parries are handled in Initiative order; if the first Parry fails, another formation member may still attempt theirs.
- A single attack may therefore have to pass through up to three Parries.

Master Parry and counterattack:
- If the weapon allows it, the formation Parry may also be a Master Parry.
- Bonus points from such a Call may be used by neighbors in the formation for the current defense or a subsequent counterattack.
- Permitted counterattack maneuvers include Wuchtschlag/Called Attack, Knockdown, and Targeted Thrust.

Polearms:
- With Spears and Infantry Weapons at least two paces long, a formation member may use Counter instead of Parry, even if they have not learned Counter.
- This can also apply against mounted attacks.

Restrictions:
- Formation members may not use maneuvers other than those explicitly allowed.
- They attack together at the Initiative phase of the slowest participant.
- Fighting in formation can still be affected by outnumbering, distance-class, and terrain rules.
- Two Blade Dancers who also know Formation may use it as a pair instead of needing at least three fighters.

defense_actions.name: Split Parry
defense_actions.base_modifier: split PA into two Parries, each PA/2 +2; declare at start of round
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver.

Blade Wall splits one Parry into two separate Parries, allowing a defender to answer two attacks in one round with fast weapon work.

Requirements:
- Requires the Blade Wall Special Ability.
- The weapon and talent must allow the maneuver.
- The fighter must be mobile enough and may not be using an incompatible shield or extra-action option.

Resolution:
- The fighter declares the split at the beginning of the combat round.
- The defender makes two Parries instead of one.
- Each Parry normally uses half the Parry Value plus 2.
- The two Parries are resolved separately and can be used against different attacks.

Restrictions:
- The split Parries normally cannot carry additional Calls such as Master Parry unless a specific rule allows it.
- They cannot be freely combined with every other extra defense source.
- Failed Calls and fumbles affect the maneuver according to the normal rules for failed maneuvers and combat fumbles.

Notes:
- Blade Wall is the defensive counterpart to Blade Storm.
- It is especially useful against Double Attack, multiple enemies, or enemies with extra attacks.

defense_actions.name: Parry with Shield
defense_actions.base_modifier: uses shield PA value and shield modifiers
defense_actions.description:
Defense Action.

A shield is used to block or deflect an incoming blow. It does not count as armor rating, even though it physically covers parts of the body.

Use:
- The fighter attacks with the weapon in the main hand but usually defends with the shield.
- The shield's Parry Value and weapon modifier are used for the defense rather than the main weapon's Parry Value.
- Optional Break Factor rules are especially important for shields, because shields can be damaged or destroyed by heavy impacts.

Restrictions:
- Some maneuvers are limited or forbidden while using a shield.
- Without Shield Combat II, many advanced defensive maneuvers such as Master Parry are not available with shields.
- Chain staves, Chain Weapons, and Whips can deny the shield's Parry weapon modifier, making shield defense worse against those weapons.

Notes:
- Shield defense is strong against ordinary blows but less flexible than weapon or parrying-weapon fencing.
- Some shields also count as parrying weapons and follow special exceptions.

defense_actions.name: Weapon Breaker
defense_actions.base_modifier: PA +8 + optional Call, then Strength test modified by weapon type and Break Factor
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver +8 + Call.

Weapon Breaker catches an incoming blade in the device of a hook dagger, left-hand dagger, dragon claw, or similar weapon and then breaks it with a forceful twist.

Requirements:
- Requires Weapon Breaker and Parrying Weapons I.
- Usable with hook dagger, suitably equipped left-hand daggers, dragon claws, or similar weapons.
- Works only against bladed weapons.
- The weapon used for breaking is usually held as a parrying weapon in the off-hand, but it can also be the main weapon.

Resolution:
- The defender makes a Parry +8 with any voluntary Call.
- If the Parry succeeds, the defender makes a Strength test.
- The Strength test is modified by the type of enemy blade and eased by the target weapon's Break Factor.
- If both tests succeed, the blade breaks and the opponent is left with only the grip or a useless remnant.

Opponent's choice:
- Once the opponent realizes what is happening, they may drop the weapon after the successful Parry but before the Strength test.
- In that case the opponent counts as disarmed, but the weapon is not broken.

Typical Strength-test modifiers:
- Longer Fencing Weapons: +4.
- Other one-handed bladed weapons, including daggers: +6.
- Two-handed bladed weapons: +10.
- Subtract the weapon's Break Factor.

defense_actions.name: Windmill
defense_actions.base_modifier: PA penalty equal to incoming maneuver penalty and Call, minimum +8; successful Parry becomes Wuchtschlag counterattack
defense_actions.description:
Defense Maneuver +8 or more.

Windmill is a risky maneuver that catches the force of a heavy incoming blow, carries it through a circular motion, and redirects it into an even stronger counterattack.

Requirements:
- Requires the Windmill Special Ability.
- Usable with Bastard Swords, Axes and Maces, Infantry Weapons, Chain Staves, Chain Weapons, Sabers, Swords, Staves, Two-Handed Flails, Two-Handed Blunt Weapons, and Two-Handed Swords/Sabers.
- A fighter using a large or very large shield cannot declare Windmill.
- The fighter must be attacked by a Wuchtschlag/Called Attack, Charge, Hammer Strike, or Cleave Attack.

Resolution:
- Windmill is performed in place of a defense action, but no conversion is required.
- It occurs in the attacker's Initiative phase.
- The defender makes a Parry with a penalty equal to the incoming maneuver's base penalty plus the attacker's voluntary Call, minimum +8.
- The required repositioning consumes a Free Action Step.

Effect on success:
- The Parry also counts as a successful Wuchtschlag/Called Attack by the defender.
- The counterattack uses a Call equal to the full penalty the defender accepted.
- The original attacker suffers a Parry penalty equal to their own original Call, as if their attack maneuver had failed.

Effect on failure:
- The defender takes full damage from the incoming attack.
- The defender also suffers the normal failed Call penalty on the next action.

Restrictions:
- Converted defense actions, partial Parries from Blade Wall, Parries with parrying weapons, and Parries from two-weapon options cannot be Windmills.
- Because it is still a Parry in principle, Break Tests for high-Call heavy attacks can apply.

defense_actions.name: Second Parrying-Weapon Parry
defense_actions.base_modifier: additional Parry once per combat round
defense_actions.description:
Defense Action.

A fighter with Parrying Weapons II may use the parrying weapon in the off-hand for one additional Parry per combat round.

Rules:
- The additional Parry cannot include further maneuvers.
- It cannot be used in the same combat round as Death from the Left with the parrying weapon.
- The fighter may still convert the main weapon's Attack action into a defense action under the normal conversion rules, allowing up to three Parries in a round.
- The use of two parrying-weapon Parries must be declared at the beginning of the combat round.
- Improvised parrying weapons do not grant this second Parry.

defense_actions.name: Second Shield Parry
defense_actions.base_modifier: additional ordinary shield Parry once per combat round
defense_actions.description:
Defense Action.

A skilled shield fighter can position the shield to block two attacks in the same combat round, whether the attacks come from one enemy or several and even when they arrive almost simultaneously.

Requirements:
- Requires Shield Combat II.
- Uses a shield in the off-hand, except tower shields.
- The fighter must be sufficiently mobile and may have at most EC 4.

Rules:
- If the fighter chooses two shield Parries, neither may be split, converted, or given a Call such as Master Parry.
- Both are ordinary shield Parries.
- The fighter may still convert the weapon Attack action into a defense action using the normal rules, allowing up to three Parries in a round.
- The use of two shield Parries must be declared at the beginning of the combat round.

free_actions.name: Orientation
free_actions.description: If a hero can concentrate and observe combat undisturbed for two actions and succeeds at an IN test, they regain INI lost due to combat and set their INI as if they had rolled a 6 at the start. Not possible if perception or movement is restricted (blinded, prone, etc.). Every 2 points in the Warcraft talent ease the IN test by 1. With Combat Awareness SA, only requires 1 action and no IN test. INI lost to wounds or active spells cannot be regained this way.

free_actions.name: Draw Weapon
free_actions.description:
Free Action / Action depending on situation.

Drawing a weapon means readying a weapon that is carried on the body. The exact time depends on how accessible the weapon is and whether the fighter has trained for quick weapon handling.

Typical handling:
- Drawing a normally worn, accessible melee weapon is often handled as a short action in combat.
- If the weapon is awkwardly stored, tied down, hidden, very large, or hard to bring into line, the GM may require a full action or more.
- Drawing while prone, kneeling, grappled, in cramped surroundings, or under poor visibility can be harder or impossible at the GM's discretion.
- Quick Draw and similar Special Abilities can reduce the required time.

Combat importance:
- A fighter without a ready weapon may be unable to Parry with it.
- Drawing a weapon at the wrong moment can provoke tactical disadvantages, especially if the enemy controls the distance.
- Changing weapons is usually slower than simply continuing with the weapon already in hand.

special_situations.name: Fighting Multiple Opponents
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

When several opponents fight one target, the single fighter cannot fully concentrate on only one enemy. Multiple-opponent rules apply to attacks, defenses, and maneuvers such as Blade Storm, Cleave Attack, Formation, Dodge, and Targeted Dodge.

Core effects:
- Additional opponents can penalize defenses; a common modifier is +1 to Parry per additional opponent, up to +2.
- Friends outnumbering the enemy can ease attacks by 1 in suitable situations.
- Ordinary Dodge or Targeted Dodge usually avoids only one attack; other attackers may still threaten the defender.
- Some maneuvers explicitly use the multiple-opponent rules and forbid focusing all attention on one target.

Tactical notes:
- Being surrounded by four or more opponents can make Dodge impossible.
- Formations and shields can partially compensate by letting allies protect one another.
- The GM should apply positioning, facing, terrain, weapon reach, and available space rather than treating all enemies as automatically able to attack at once.

special_situations.name: Fumble
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

A combat fumble is a disastrous attack or defense roll, usually connected to a natural 20 and then resolved using the combat fumble rules or table. It represents more than a simple miss: losing balance, overextending, exposing oneself, damaging the weapon, or creating an opening.

Common consequences:
- Initiative loss.
- A worsened position or loss of footing.
- Dropping or damaging a weapon.
- Granting the opponent an immediate tactical opportunity.
- In some cases, weapon or shield stress may call for a Break Test.

Interaction with maneuvers:
- Maneuvers with Calls still apply the normal failed Call penalty when they fail.
- In Double Attack, if one partial attack is a fumble, the other partial attack automatically fails as well.
- The GM should distinguish an ordinary failed attack from a true fumble; a miss may simply be late, weak, or deflected, while a fumble creates a real complication.

special_situations.name: Prone Fighter
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

A fighter may end up kneeling or prone after a fall, a leap into cover, a failed maneuver, a fumble, or a successful knockdown-style attack. The fighter can spend actions to stand up, or continue fighting from the bad position.

Changing position:
- Changing from prone to kneeling, or kneeling to standing, requires one Action Position and no test.
- Going directly from prone to standing in one action requires a Dexterity/Agility-style test penalized by full Encumbrance and still uses an Action Position.

Prone fighter:
- Attacks and Parries are penalized by +3.
- Targeted Dodge and Orientation cannot be used.
- Other activities such as drawing a weapon may be harder or impossible depending on the situation.
- Attacks against a prone target are easier: AT -3 and PA -5 for the attacker.

Kneeling fighter:
- Attacks and Parries are penalized by +1.
- Dodge is penalized by +4.
- Some maneuvers may be impossible depending on weapon, reach, and exact circumstances.
- Attacks against a kneeling target are easier: AT -1 and PA -3 for the attacker.

special_situations.name: Off-hand Combat
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

Using the off-hand or fighting with weapons in both hands is difficult unless trained. The normal rules assume a dominant hand; using the wrong hand imposes major penalties that Special Abilities reduce.

Wrong-hand use:
- A weapon used in the wrong hand normally suffers +9 to Attack and +9 to Parry.
- Linkhand reduces this penalty by 3.
- Ambidextrous Combat I reduces it by another 3.
- Ambidextrous Combat II reduces it by another 3, effectively removing the normal wrong-hand penalty.
- A HP/ST bonus with the wrong hand can only be used if the fighter has Ambidextrous Combat I.

Two-weapon implications:
- Extra attacks or parries from the off-hand follow their own rules and cannot always be combined with other maneuvers.
- Double Attack, Death from the Left, extra parrying-weapon parries, and shield parries are mutually restricted in several cases.
- If only one of a fighter's weapons is bound, disarmed, or otherwise controlled, the other may still be available unless the specific maneuver says otherwise.

special_situations.name: Mounted Combat
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

Mounted combat changes movement, reach, initiative, attacks, defenses, and many maneuver options. The rider must control both their own weapon and the mount's movement.

General handling:
- Riding tests are used at the start of combat to determine how well the rider controls the mount and gains combat options.
- Further Riding tests may be required after the rider or mount is hit; failure can mean reduced options or falling from the saddle.
- Armor encumbrance is treated more favorably on horseback: effective encumbrance is generally reduced compared with foot combat.
- Jousting/lance-riding follows its own attack procedure and is not simply a normal melee attack.

Typical modifiers to Riding tests include:
- Untrained, inexperienced, tested, or trained horse.
- No saddle or stirrups.
- Steering without hands.
- Charging several opponents.
- Rider encumbrance and wounds.
- Wounds to the mount.
- Damage suffered by rider or mount.
- Difficult terrain.

Tactical notes:
- Mounted fighters can use speed and reach to gain strong attack positions.
- A hit against rider or mount can quickly change the fight by forcing tests or causing a fall.
- Some Special Abilities reduce mounted-combat penalties or improve lance-riding.

special_situations.name: Break Test
special_situations.description:
Special Combat Situation.

A Break Test checks whether a weapon or shield survives extreme stress. It is relevant after especially heavy blows, strong Parries, shield impacts, weapon-breaking maneuvers, and other situations where the rules call for item breakage.

When it can occur:
- Powerful attacks with high Calls, such as Hammer Strike or other Wuchtschlag-based maneuvers.
- Shield Splitter or other attacks directed at equipment.
- Windmill and similar defensive maneuvers that absorb and redirect a heavy blow.
- Weapon Breaker and other techniques that directly try to destroy a blade.

Resolution:
- Roll according to the item's Break Factor rules.
- Modifiers from the maneuver, weapon type, shield type, or attack strength are applied.
- If the test fails, the item breaks or is destroyed as specified by the rule.

Notes:
- Shields are especially likely to be checked if the optional Break Factor rules are used.
- The GM should apply Break Tests only when the maneuver or situation calls for them; ordinary successful Parries do not automatically destroy equipment.
